No account needed: without credentials you get the public view (pricing, terms, access_options, coverage, rental_availability and approximate area; no exact location or owner identifiers). tools.name: whoami

Used for operator decisions on your listings and lease requests, and for lease inquiries and host responses. Same rules as at registration; works while you

tools.name: request_lease
tools.description: Request a time-boxed rental of an available robot. Select an offered access_type or omit it for the primary rental arrangement. Personnel-operated and equipment-only rentals require empty granted_permissions and mint no control token. Remote controls require configured integration and permitted scop

tools.name: activate_lease
tools.description: Activate your confirmed rental within its time window. Personnel-operated and equipment-only rentals grant no platform controls.

tools.name: cancel_lease
tools.description: Cancel one of your leases before it goes ACTIVE (REQUESTED or CONFIRMED). Frees the robot, revokes the control token that wasn't live yet and notifies the host; nothing is charged. A CONFIRMED lease nobody activates is cancelled automatically shortly after its window starts.

tools.name: return_lease
tools.description: End one of your ACTIVE leases and hand the robot back. finding is 'clean' or 'damage'.

tools.name: open_control_session
tools.description: Only for an ACTIVE configured remote-control rental. Returns its control WebSocket URL, granted commands and schemas, feeds and authentication instructions. Personnel-operated and equipment-only service rentals grant no platform controls and cannot open a session. Supervisory clients may alternative

tools.name: get_robot_status
tools.description: Read-only. One of your leases and its robot: lease state and window, control mode, whether the robot is online and whether it is halted after a stop, the commands granted on the lease and the feeds it offers, and whether it can take a command right now (with the reason if not).

tools.name: list_robot_commands
tools.description: Read-only. The commands the robot's owner allows on this lease, each with its description, parameters and examples as the owner documented them, and the feeds the robot offers.

tools.name: send_robot_command
tools.description: Runs one command on the leased robot and returns the robot's result. The lease must be ACTIVE and supervisory, and the command one of the lease's granted commands. The robot acts in the physical world. An idempotency_key makes a retry safe: the same key returns the first result instead of acting aga

tools.name: get_camera_frame
tools.description: Read-only. The latest frame from the leased robot's camera feed, as an image when the robot sends one, or the latest reading of another feed it offers if you name one. The lease must be ACTIVE and supervisory. A sensor fault is reported and leaves the lease running.

tools.name: create_inquiry
tools.description: Ask a body owner about robot availability, pricing, delivery or rental requirements. Include a requested window and your message. Required first for listings whose rental_availability is on_request. Works for service rentals and offered remote arrangements before integration is ready. Reserves nothi

tools.name: list_inquiries
tools.description: The inquiries you sent, newest first, with the host's answer when there is one. Optional status filter.

tools.name: get_inquiry
tools.description: One inquiry (renter or host), including its promise if one was made.

tools.name: accept_inquiry
tools.description: Renter only, inquiry must be offered: pick one offered window by window_index. Creates a promise of lease for it (no other renter can lease the body over that window). Redeem it with request_lease and promise_id when the window opens.

tools.name: cancel_inquiry
tools.description: Withdraw an inquiry you sent that is still open or offered, or cancel a promise you accepted.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_bodies, open_control_session, get_robot_status, list_robot_commands, get_camera_frame, create_inquiry · Private data: find_robot_for_task, list_bodies, request_lease, cancel_lease · Public sink: list_bodies, whoami, update_notification, send_robot_command.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_bodies, open_control_session, get_robot_status, list_robot_commands, get_camera_frame, create_inquiry · Private data: find_robot_for_task, list_bodies, request_lease, cancel_lease · Public sink: list_bodies, whoami, update_notification, send_robot_command

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
